answer: CIVE 536 Hydrology, 3(3,0): precipitation data, flood analysis, evaporation and transpiration, streamflow measurement, groundwater hydrology, rainfall-runoff and statistical hydrology.

source_quote: Quality and control tests for water and wastewater, design principles of water and
answer: CIVE 538 Water and Wastewater Treatment, 3(3,0): water and wastewater quality tests, treatment plant design principles, and physical, chemical and biological processes. Prerequisites: CIVE 432 and CIVE 435.

answer: CIVE 595A BE Summative Learning Project 1, 1(1,0): first part of the team BE project on an approved specialty topic - literature review, scope of work and project proposal. Prerequisites: Senior Standing and ENGL 217.

answer: CIVE 595B BE Summative Learning Project 2, 3(3,0): second part of the team BE project - design, data collection, experimentation, analysis and technical writing. Prerequisite: CIVE 595A.

source_quote: Elements of set theory, basic elements of probability theory, random variables,
answer: CIVE 502 Engineering Risk Analysis, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective: probability, random variables, probabilistic models, statistical inference and reliability formulation. Prerequisite: MATH 351.

source_quote: Using the computer for analysis, design, and decision making in civil engineering.
answer: CIVE 503 Computer Methods in Civil Engineering, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective: computer-based analysis and design, converting CAD/REVIT elements to structural elements, shop drawings and value engineering. Prerequisite: Senior Standing.

source_quote: Problems of infrastructure, asset management principles, methods of inspection and
answer: CIVE 504 Infrastructure Asset Management, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective: asset management principles, inspection and monitoring, risk assessment, condition data and replace/maintain decisions. Prerequisite: Senior Standing.

source_quote: Green construction methods and benefits of applying the Leadership in Energy and
answer: CIVE 506 LEED and Green Construction Principles in Construction Management, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective: green construction methods and LEED principles. Prerequisite: Senior Standing.

source_quote: vary each time the course is offered, and the course content will be available with
answer: CIVE 597 Topics in Civil Engineering, 3(3,0): special-interest topics that vary by offering; may be repeated for credit as topics vary. Prerequisite: consent of advisor.

source_quote: Theory of the finite element method; spring, truss, and beam elements; constant-
answer: CIVE 510 Finite Elements Analysis, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): finite element theory, spring/truss/beam and constant-strain elements, plane stress/strain, plates and shells, nonlinear and dynamic analysis intro. Prerequisite: CIVE 312.

source_quote: Dynamic response of single- and multi-degree-of-freedom systems; modal analysis
answer: CIVE 511 Structural Dynamics, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): SDOF/MDOF dynamic response, modal analysis, natural frequencies, response spectra and seismic design principles. Prerequisite: CIVE 312.

source_quote: Flexibility and Stiffness Matrix Methods for Analysis of Indeterminate Trusses, Beams,
answer: CIVE 512 Advanced Structural Analysis, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): flexibility and stiffness matrix methods, grids, elastic supports, composite systems and influence lines for indeterminate structures. Prerequisite: CIVE 507.

source_quote: Earthquake causes and measures; earthquake faults and waves; plate tectonics;
answer: CIVE 514 Earthquake Engineering, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): earthquake causes, faults and waves, structural dynamics, seismic hazard, response analysis, equivalent static lateral force method and mitigation. Prerequisite: CIVE 312.

source_quote: Definitions and Methods of prestressing. Materials and their properties. Discussion of
answer: CIVE 515 Prestressed Concrete, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): prestressing methods and materials, losses, stress analysis and design, shear cracking, load balancing, deflection, shrinkage and creep. Prerequisite: CIVE 314.

source_quote: Loadings; structural systems and analysis modeling; braced frames; rigid frame
answer: CIVE 519 Tall Building Structures, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): loading, structural systems, braced and rigid frames, stability, dynamic response, shear walls and dual systems. Prerequisite: CIVE 413.

source_quote: Design and characteristics of lightweight concrete, heavyweight concrete, self-
answer: CIVE 521 Special Concretes, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): lightweight, heavyweight, self-consolidating, fiber-reinforced, mass, high-strength and roller-compacted concretes and hot/cold weather concreting. Prerequisite: CIVE 321.

source_quote: Definition and importance of durability; properties of main building materials (concrete,
answer: CIVE 522 Durability of Construction Materials, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): durability of concrete, metals, wood, stone, brick and other materials, decay mechanisms, durability tests and economics. Prerequisite: CIVE 321.

source_quote: Conventional methods of investigation; nondestructive methods; structural health
answer: CIVE 523 Repair of Concrete Structures, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): investigation and nondestructive methods, corrosion evaluation and protection, repair materials, crack repair, patching and strengthening. Prerequisite: CIVE 321.

source_quote: Overview of the different types of civil infrastructure, their problems and durability, use
answer: CIVE 524 Nondestructive Evaluation & Instrumentation of Infrastructure, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): NDE methods (ultrasonic, GPR, infrared, resistivity, nuclear), sensors, wireless technology and structural health monitoring. Prerequisite: CIVE 321.

source_quote: Cement and supplementary cementitious materials, mechanical behavior of concrete,
answer: CIVE 525 Concrete Technology, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (annually): cements, concrete behavior, specialized concretes, admixtures, mix proportioning, and deterioration (alkali-aggregate reaction, carbonation, chloride and sulfate attack, freeze-thaw). Prerequisite: CIVE 321.

source_quote: Definition and classification of concrete admixtures; precautions in their use;
answer: CIVE 526 Admixtures for Concrete, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): classification, types, standards, mechanisms and effects of chemical and mineral admixtures on fresh and hardened concrete. Prerequisite: CIVE 321.

source_quote: rock dams. Prerequisite: CIVE 424; Co-requisite: CIVE 536. On demand.
answer: CIVE 527 Seepage and Dams, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): hydraulic conductivity, seepage analysis and control, wells, filters and drains, and earth and earth-rock dams. Prerequisite: CIVE 424; co-requisite: CIVE 536.

source_quote: Types of earth-retaining systems; earth pressure theory; design of externally
answer: CIVE 528 Earth Retaining Structures, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): earth pressure theory, externally and internally stabilized walls and soil reinforcement. Prerequisites: CIVE 424 and CIVE 314.

source_quote: Lateral earth pressure, retaining walls, sheet-pile walls, anchors, braced cuts, drilled-
answer: CIVE 529 Advanced Foundation Engineering, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): lateral earth pressure, retaining and sheet-pile walls, anchors, braced cuts, drilled shafts, problematic soils, rock foundations and soil improvement. Prerequisite: CIVE 424.

source_quote: Water quality parameters; sources of drinking water; drinking water problems and
answer: CIVE 571 Water Quality, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): water quality parameters, drinking water sources and treatment, distribution system design and water quality monitoring. Prerequisite: CIVE 432.

source_quote: Study of the types and sources of non-hazardous municipal solid waste; estimation of
answer: CIVE 573 Solid Waste Management, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): municipal solid waste types and quantities, collection, transfer, treatment and disposal, preliminary landfill design and pollution control. Prerequisite: CIVE 432.

source_quote: Identification and evaluation of water supply solutions; design of water distribution
answer: CIVE 575 Water Supply & Wastewater Systems, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): water supply solutions, distribution network design, pumping, population forecasting, storm and sewage system design. Prerequisite: CIVE 435.

source_quote: Hydraulic aspects of the theory and design of hydraulic structures; types of dams and
answer: CIVE 576 Hydraulic Structures, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): design of hydraulic structures, dams and gravity dam stability, culverts, canals, reservoirs, ports, gates and weirs. Prerequisites: CIVE 435 and CIVE 536.

source_quote: Review of basic cartographic principles and the use of geographic information
answer: CIVE 540 GIS for Civil Engineering, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): cartography and GIS for thematic mapping and spatial analysis in water resources, with GIS software labs. Prerequisite: Senior Standing.

source_quote: Analysis and design of flexible and rigid pavements; pavement type selection; loading;
answer: CIVE 541 Pavement Design, 3(3,0), a civil technical elective (on demand): flexible and rigid pavement analysis and design, type selection, loading, failure criteria, reliability and mechanistic design. Prerequisite: CIVE 423.
